name: HGH Fragment 176-191

lead: HGH Fragment 176-191 is a 16-amino-acid peptide corresponding to the C-terminal end of human growth hormone. It is sold as a research chemical and promoted for fat loss on the idea that it keeps growth hormone's lipolytic action without its other effects.

Published data are largely preclinical, and no completed controlled human trials of this exact peptide support its marketing claims. Its modified relative AOD-9604 did reach human trials but fell short on efficacy.

paras: In cell and rodent studies the fragment appears to stimulate lipolysis and reduce lipogenesis in fat tissue, apparently without activating the growth hormone receptor pathways that raise IGF-1 or blood glucose. The exact receptor mechanism is not well defined.

Human safety data are essentially absent for this specific peptide. It is unapproved for medical use, supplied by unregulated sources with unverified purity, and listed as prohibited by WADA among growth hormone fragments. Efficacy for human fat loss is unproven.
